accepted_claims: For fixed kappa>0, degree zero, and j in the credited interval (4*pi,4*pi+epsilon_kappa), e(j) is continuous and locally semiconcave, hence locally Lipschitz; all constrained minimizers over compact subintervals form a strongly H1 compact family.
For every degree-zero H1 field with |J|>4*pi, the smooth pointwise-rotation momentum derivative is onto R3. Weak equivariance and finite-energy endpoint limits give the rank obstruction |J|=4*pi.

Every minimizing field has a unique weak variational vector multiplier alpha=omega*a. Exact finite-dimensional corrections yield continuous multipliers and uniformly bounded quadratic upper supports on compact subintervals.

The finite one-sided derivatives satisfy e_right_prime(j)=min over M(j) of omega and e_left_prime(j)=max over M(j) of omega. Extrema are attained, and every minimizing multiplier equals e_prime(j) at differentiability points.

Under the declared positive joint-rotation and Landau-Lifshitz conventions, a smooth minimizing profile generates frequency omega and is static exactly when omega=0. The missing nonzero-multiplier conclusion is not established.
not_claimed: A solution of the original non-staticity or quantitative-energy problem; the original target remains OPEN.
